title: Quality Control
outcomes: Explain audit quality and the SQC 1 system of quality control.
Apply SA 220 responsibilities at engagement level.
Describe engagement quality control review and documentation.
Explain peer review, QRB and NFRA oversight.

meta.exam_tip: Case studies: identify the element breached, cite SQC 1 or SA 220, and state the corrective step.

concepts.title: Audit quality and SQC 1 at firm level
body: Audit quality means a rigorous process that complies with laws and professional standards, giving users trust in the opinion. SQC 1 sets the firm-wide system of quality control for audits, reviews, other assurance and related services; SA 220 applies it to each audit engagement.

SQC 1 elements: leadership responsibilities for quality (tone at the top, quality over commercial pressure); relevant ethical requirements including independence (annual confirmations, threats and safeguards, rotation for long associations with listed clients); acceptance and continuance of clients (integrity, competence, ability to comply with ethics); human resources (recruitment, training, assignment); engagement performance (direction, supervision, review, consultation, differences of opinion, EQCR); and monitoring (periodic inspection of completed engagements).
Status: ICAI issued SQM 1, SQM 2 and revised SA 220 in October 2024, but in March 2026 it deferred their mandatory date until further announcement, so SQC 1 continues to apply.
concepts.analogy: Quality starts at the top and runs through six linked elements.
concepts.work: A firm rewarding partners only for fee growth fails the leadership element.

concepts.title: SA 220: quality control on each audit
body: The engagement partner takes responsibility for overall audit quality: complying with ethics and independence, being satisfied with acceptance and continuance procedures, ensuring the team collectively has the right competence and time, and directing, supervising and reviewing the work.
The partner ensures appropriate consultation on difficult or contentious matters, that conclusions are implemented, and that differences of opinion are resolved before the report is dated.
Monitoring results from the firm are considered, and the partner remains alert to non-compliance with ethical requirements by team members.
concepts.analogy: Each audit has one partner accountable for its quality.
concepts.work: A partner must consult the firm's technical team on a contentious Ind AS issue.

concepts.title: Engagement quality control review and documentation
body: An engagement quality control review (EQCR) is an objective evaluation, before the report is issued, of significant judgements made by the team and conclusions reached. It is required for audits of listed entities and other engagements meeting the firm's criteria.

The reviewer considers the team's independence evaluation, significant risks and responses, judgements on materiality and significant risks, consultations, the appropriateness of the report, and documentation. The reviewer must be objective and suitably qualified, not part of the team.

Documentation shows compliance with ethics and independence, acceptance conclusions, consultations, and that the EQCR was completed before the report date. Audit files are assembled within 60 days of the report date and retained for at least seven years (SQC 1).
concepts.analogy: A second, independent senior look before signing.
concepts.work: The report cannot be dated before the EQCR is completed.

concepts.title: External review: Peer Review Board, Quality Review Board and NFRA
body: The Peer Review Board of ICAI reviews practice units periodically to check compliance with technical standards and quality control, issuing a peer review certificate; certain audits (e.g. listed entities) require a valid certificate.
The Quality Review Board (set up by the Central Government under the CA Act) reviews the quality of audit services and recommends improvements, guiding members.

The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), under the Companies Act, recommends accounting and auditing standards, monitors compliance, oversees the quality of service of auditors of listed and large companies, and can investigate and impose penalties.
concepts.analogy: Firms are reviewed by peers, by QRB and, for big companies, by NFRA.
concepts.work: NFRA can debar an auditor for professional misconduct in a listed company audit.

illustrations.title: Which SQC 1 element is weak?
illustrations.q: In R & Co., (a) partners push for fee growth regardless of risk; (b) a staff member holds shares in an audit client; (c) a client with doubtful integrity was accepted without enquiry; (d) juniors with no bank experience are sent to a bank audit; (e) working papers are not reviewed before signing; (f) no one checks whether firm policies are followed. Map each to the element of quality control.

cases.title: Sharma & Associates
cases.case: Sharma & Associates audits a listed textile company. The engagement partner signed the report on 20 May; the EQCR reviewer completed her review on 22 May. A team senior's spouse holds shares in the client. The firm's last peer review certificate expired in March.
